newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur to hold to five pct limit rule.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur to hold to five pct limit rule.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co plans to hold to its rule of allowing no shareholder to enter more than five percent of the company's stock in its register despite the recent activity surrounding its shares, chief executive Peter Spaelti said.

"We can exercise no influence over purchases on the bourse...On the other hand our board has stated clearly that it wants to hold the statutory registration limit of Winterthur's capital," Spaelti said in an interview published in the Saturday edition of the Swiss daily Tages Anzieger.
"Therefore we will also in future enter no shareholder with more than five percent," he added.
Winterthur was the centre of attention on the Swiss exchange on Friday following the revelation that Swiss Reinsurance had accumulated about about five percent of Winterthur's outstanding shares.

The size of the Swiss Re stake was made public by Swiss financier Martin Ebner who also said on Thursday that his BZ Group of investment funds had raised its stake in Winterthur to 18.3 percent as of June 30 from 14.5 percent in mid-May.
Ebner has said he wants to be a long-term oriented Winterthur shareholder and Winterthur is holding to this statement, Spaelti said in the interview.

Commenting further, Spaelti said Swiss Re has been a Winterthur shareholder for some time and that as a larger investor, it divides its investments more or less according to the weightings of the various stocks in the share index.
Winterthur has a weighting of about two percent in the Swiss market, he said.

He also said Credit Suisse Group and Commerzbank AG both hold considerably less than five percent of Winterthur's shares and that the five percent limit restriction would also hold for these two investors.
Spaelti told a Swiss radio interviewer on Friday that he had heard nothing about any possible takeover offer for his company from Swiss Re or from Credit Suisse.
